---
title: "Pico"
subtitle: "Building your first Pico."
---

Welcome to **Pico**, the reference course of the Open Engineering Academy.
This course teaches how to design and build your first Pico — a small,
declarative, composable engineering artifact — and doubles as the canonical
example for how every academy course website is structured.

## Where this course fits

Pico is the academy's **behaviour** layer. The three-layer story is:

> **Crossplane composes**, **Sandcastle constructs**, **Picos behave**.

This course teaches what a Pico *does* at runtime — how a `hello-world-pico`
receives events, evaluates rules, and produces actions. Its sibling courses
teach the other two layers:

- [Crossplane course](../crossplane/index.html) — declares and composes what
  should exist on a control plane.
- [Sandcastle course](../sandcastle/index.html) — the bounded engineering
  environment inside which artifacts like Picos are safely built.

Pico is the foundation for the other two: complete this course first so you
know what a durable Pico artifact looks like before you compose it with
Crossplane or construct it inside a Sandcastle.

## What you will learn

By the end of the course you will be able to:

- Explain what a Pico is and how it fits into Open Engineering.
- Author Rules, a Parser, and a Composer for a minimal Pico.
- Produce a working `hello-world-pico` and describe it with metadata.
- Distinguish a Pico's **Mind** (whether/why it should act) from its
  **Hands** (how an action is executed), and explain why Hands stay
  provider-neutral. See
  [Part 3 · Hands](part-3/05-hands/index.qmd).
- Place a Pico's
  [**Nervous System**](glossary.qmd#nervous-system) *after* Hands in the
  Pico progression and distinguish Brain/Mind, Hands, **Voice** (what a
  Pico communicates outward), and the transport-neutral fabric those
  messages travel through. The course defines provider-neutral message
  semantics — envelope, observation, event, command, delegation,
  result, presence, discovery, and topic/capability authorization —
  before naming MQTT or EMQX as candidate transport implementations.
  See
  [Constructive realization · Nervous system as a governed extension](constructive-realization.qmd#nervous-system-as-a-governed-extension).

See the course descriptor in [`metadata.yaml`](metadata.yaml) for the
machine-readable summary (id, level, duration, prerequisites, teaches,
produces).

## Six-module course spine

The course spine follows the capsule-first module progression proposed in
[`memo23.md`](../../memo23.md) §4. Each row names a module, summarises
what it teaches in one line taken from memo23 §4, and points at the
material in this repository today — or marks the module as **not yet
available** when it depends on an upstream contract that has not been
committed (see
[`memo24.md`](../../memo24.md) §2.1).

| # | Module | Teach (one line, memo23 §4) | Where it lives today |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Understand a Pico | What a Pico is and the four terms *capability*, *capsule definition*, *capsule implementation*, *composed Pico*. | [Part 1 lesson 1 — Understand a Pico](part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd) and the shared [`labs/hello-pico/`](../../labs/hello-pico/) lab. |
| 2 | Define a capsule | Capsule metadata and contract boundaries using the canonical capsule definition format. | Not yet available — waits on the upstream capsule contract ([`memo24.md`](../../memo24.md) §2.1, [`memo26.md`](../../memo26.md)). |
| 3 | Implement and test a capsule | Implement one capability behind its contract with dependencies kept local; add unit and contract tests. | Not yet available — waits on the upstream capsule contract ([`memo24.md`](../../memo24.md) §2.1, [`memo26.md`](../../memo26.md)). |
| 4 | Compose a Pico | Declarative composition of capsule capabilities; dependency resolution, interface binding, version compatibility, validation. | Not yet available — waits on the upstream capsule contract ([`memo24.md`](../../memo24.md) §2.1, [`memo26.md`](../../memo26.md)). |
| 5 | Run and inspect the Pico | The boundary between composition and execution; runtime responsibilities, lifecycle, logging, health, failure handling. | Partially covered by [`labs/hello-pico/`](../../labs/hello-pico/) (the smallest supported run path, per memo23 §9 step 3); the full capsule-aware runtime path waits on the same upstream contract. |
| 6 | Extend and operate the Pico | Add one optional capability (persistence, event adapter, tool integration, bot interface) without redesigning the core. | [Part 3 — Extending](part-3/index.qmd) lessons 1–6 and their matched extension labs (`labs/hello-pico-hands-kubernetes/`, `labs/hello-pico-nervous-system-mqtt/`, and the Manifold/Crossplane labs under `labs/`). |

Modules 2–4 are intentionally **not yet runnable** in this course. They
depend on a canonical capsule contract that is not yet committed to
`open-engineering-capsules/source` (verified
2026-10-16, [`memo24.md`](../../memo24.md) §2.1). This course will
consume that contract when the owning repository publishes it; it does
not define a second, course-specific one.

## Zero-optional-platform path

The shortest ordered walk a learner can complete today with **no**
Kubernetes, no cluster, no broker, no Composio, no Home Assistant, no
Sandcastle, no Crossplane, no `gh`/Flux, and no live hosted dependency
— only a shell, a text editor, Python 3, and the in-repo `bin/pico` CLI
— is (from [`memo25.md`](../../memo25.md) "Minimal zero-optional-platform
path"):

1. [Part 1 lesson 1 — Understand a Pico](part-1/01-introduction/index.qmd).
2. [Part 1 lesson 1 — Exercise](part-1/01-introduction/exercise.qmd).
3. [Part 1 lesson 1 — Lab](part-1/01-introduction/lab.qmd) → the shared [`labs/hello-pico/`](../../labs/hello-pico/) lab.
4. [`labs/hello-pico/`](../../labs/hello-pico/) — author one Rule, run `pico parse` → `pico compose`, execute `./build/hello-world-pico` (the memo23 §9 step-3 minimum path).
5. [Part 1 lesson 1 — Summary](part-1/01-introduction/summary.qmd) and [Quiz](part-1/01-introduction/quiz.qmd).
6. [Part 2 — Building](part-2/index.qmd) (read-only scaffold explaining Modules 2–5 are reserved).
7. [Part 3 lesson 1 — Pico Identity](part-3/01-pico-identity/index.qmd), [lesson 2 — Cross-Mesh Communication](part-3/02-cross-mesh-communication/index.qmd), [lesson 3 — Trust and Authorization](part-3/03-trust-and-authorization/index.qmd) and their `pico parse`-only labs.
8. Optional: [Part 3 lesson 4 — Portability](part-3/04-portability/index.qmd) and its lab (adds a `bash` verification script, no platform).
9. Optional: [Part 3 lesson 5 — Hands](part-3/05-hands/index.qmd) + its lab and [lesson 6 — Nervous System](part-3/06-nervous-system/index.qmd) + its lab (both validate governance artefacts with Python 3 + PyYAML, no network). A learner on the zero-optional path can read these but should **skip** each lesson's sidebar link to its "runnable Kubernetes" or MQTT lab until they choose to add that platform — see [Part 3 — Extending](part-3/index.qmd) for the explicit skip list.

Everything else (the Manifold/Wrangler, Crossplane, Composio, Home
Assistant, EMQX/MQTT, Sandcastle, and outer-delivery labs) requires at
least one optional platform and belongs on the extension path per
[`memo25.md`](../../memo25.md).

## How this course is structured

The course is organized into **parts**, each part into **lessons**, and each
lesson into a consistent set of pages:

```
courses/pico/
  _quarto.yml          # this course website
  index.qmd            # you are here
  metadata.yaml        # machine-readable course descriptor
  glossary.qmd         # course glossary
  part-1/              # section
    index.qmd
    01-introduction/   # lesson
      index.qmd
      exercise.qmd
      lab.qmd
      summary.qmd
      quiz.qmd
      assets/
  part-2/
  part-3/
  labs/                # course-scoped labs
  assets/              # course-scoped assets
```
